title: Okavango Delta Formation
summary: The Okavango Delta is a large, low-gradient alluvial fan in north-western Botswana, built where the Okavango River spreads into a fault-bounded graben linked to the East African Rift system; its water drains into the Kalahari sands, not the sea. Its age is unresolved: IRD cites estimates from 12,000 years to 2 million years, while luminescence dating puts the start of alluvial-fan deposition in the incised rift no later than about 250,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Age is contested. IRD gives an estimated age between 12,000 years and 2 million years. Vainer et al. (2024, via Ben-Gurion University) date eolian sand formation to ~2.2-1.1 Ma, place major rift subsidence after that (latest major deformation probably 1.2-0.75 Ma), and date the start of alluvial-fan deposition to no later than ~250 ka. The pin year uses the 250 ka minimum; the id's 2 Ma is only a lookup key.

as_recorded.value: estimated between 12,000 years and 2 million years

when.display: Uncertain: estimates from c. 2 million to 12,000 years ago; fan deposition under way by c. 250,000 years ago

where.historical_name: Okavango Rift Zone, Kalahari Basin (before any polity)

importance.justification: Formed Africa's largest endorheic delta, a UNESCO World Heritage wetland, through rift faulting in the Kalahari.
